key_insight: MultiGP exploits the fact that different objects in the same scene share one illumination to resolve the inherently ambiguous separation of reflectance, texture, and lighting from a single image, producing stochastic samples of plausible radiometric explanations.
problem_solved: Disentangling material (reflectance & texture) and illumination from a single image is highly underconstrained and ambiguous; the paper addresses this by using multi-object consensus to reliably infer all radiometric constituents.
method: Generative inverse-rendering framework that stochastically samples the latent radiometric factors (reflectance, texture, illumination) consistent with an input image.
Enforces cross-object illumination consensus: objects in the same scene share a single illumination hypothesis, which constrains and disambiguates per-object material estimates.
Produces diverse plausible explanations (uncertainty-aware outputs) rather than a single deterministic estimate, enabling robust downstream use.
impact: Enables more accurate and uncertainty-aware estimation of materials and lighting from single photos, improving tasks like relighting, realistic object insertion, AR, and material-aware scene understanding for AI/ML practitioners.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: single input image → generative sampler → separate outputs for reflectance, texture, and shared illumination.
Consensus illustration: multiple objects in a scene pointing to a single shared illumination estimate that disambiguates their materials.
Result panel: several stochastic renderings showing different plausible decompositions and relit reconstructions.
Before/after examples: original image next to edited relit or material-modified versions to demonstrate practical uses.
paper_title: Under One Sun: Multi-Object Generative Perception of Materials and Illumination
paper_authors: Nobuo Yoshii, Xinran Nicole Han, Ryo Kawahara, Todd Zickler, Ko Nishino
